description: The bar chart illustrates the average number of likes received by posts grouped according to the angular similarity of their headlines, as measured in degrees, with the x-axis labeled “Most similar group of posts” and categorized into five intervals: (0,90], (90,180], (180,270], (270,360], and (360,450]. The y-axis, labeled “Avg. Like #”, ranges from 400 to 600 in increments of 50, representing the average number of likes per post group. Each bar is a solid gray rectangle with vertical error bars indicating variability. The first group, (0,90], has the highest average likes at approximately 600. The second group, (90,180], drops to about 565. The third group, (180,270], rises slightly to around 575. The fourth group, (270,360], is near 595, and the fifth group, (360,450], settles at approximately 585. The bars are not sorted by height, and no bars are visually emphasized beyond their uniform color and error bars. The chart suggests that posts with headline similarities in the lowest angular range (0–90 degrees) tend to receive the most likes on average, while those in the 90–180 degree range receive the fewest.
